title: Building an MCP Server — Python + TypeScript SDKs

questions.question: A team wants its customer lookup available to every assistant in the company. What is the first structural decision?
options: Which assistant host to hardcode it into first
What color the lookup button should be
How many copies to maintain per team
Expose it once as a server on the shared contract, then connect each host
questions.explanation: One server on the shared contract serves every host. This lesson builds that server: capabilities, dispatch, and tool handlers.

questions.question: What does a successful notes_create call return besides its confirmation text?
options: Only a numeric database id
a resource block at notes://<new-id>
A prompt named review_note with no note
A shutdown response
questions.explanation: Creating a note returns text plus a resource block pointing at the newly created notes:// URI.

questions.question: What does dispatch return for a notification with no id?
options: A response with id null for every notification
The server's entire tool registry
None
A -32601 error even for known methods
questions.explanation: Notifications are deliberately one-way; dispatch does not emit a JSON-RPC response when the id is absent.

questions.question: What happens when resources_read receives an unknown notes:// URI?
options: It returns the first note as a fallback
It silently creates the requested note
It returns a prompt message
ValueError, mapped by dispatch to -32603
questions.explanation: The resource reader rejects an unknown URI; the dispatcher turns that handler exception into an internal-error response.

questions.question: What is the observable result of calling notes_search with query MCP?
options: JSON text containing matching notes
It always returns an empty binary resource
It creates a new note before searching
It raises because query must be a number
questions.explanation: The search lowercases the query, finds matching title/body text, and serializes the hit list into a text content block.

questions.question: Which argument is required by the review_note prompt?
options: tag
note_id
units
targetLength
questions.explanation: prompts_list declares review_note with the required note_id argument; prompt retrieval uses that id to build the user message.
